answer: Metered bandwidth receipts. An archive serving plume images, sonnet recordings, and glacier scans can require a fresh incompressible upload for each rewarded slot. The verifier supplies an unpredictable stream bound to the account and epoch, measures bytes received, and consumes its receipt once. N slots require N separate transfers, costing bandwidth and network capacity even under one operator. This assumes an honest remote meter; accepting only a hash or allowing stream reuse would let many accounts share one transfer.
